title: Backpressure mismatch causing queue delay amplification and retry storms - fix + escalation playbook
creator: Ava Nguyen
description:
Summary: During a customer escalation window (multi-tenant surge), hosted inference observed cascading timeouts and 5xx rates caused by an amplification loop between the edge proxy and the runtime. The proxy continued accepting and buffering requests while the runtime entered long tail latency due to KV cache eviction and long-context batches; clients retried, amplifying load. Dedicated pools experienced less cross-tenant noise but showed similar stall patterns when autoscale lagged. Private deployments surfaced persistent timeouts related to network egress limits + the same backpressure semantics mismatch.

Why this is unique: previous tickets focused on retry throttles or connection pools; this issue is primarily a semantic mismatch in backpressure signals (proxy inflight semantics vs runtime admission) leading to queue-length amplification and retry storms.

Immediate impact: customer-visible 5xx spikes for affected tenants, high retry counts, increased token cost due to repeat work, and degraded latency SLOs for synchronous generation endpoints.
acceptance_criteria: Proxy-to-runtime backpressure alignment implemented and tested in staging
No customer-visible 5xx spikes during a synthetic tenant surge (run at 2x observed blast) for 1 hour
p95/p99 latency and retry-per-request metrics return to baseline within rollout window
Edge rate-limiter and per-tenant fastfail in place and documented in runbook
steps: Mitigation (0-2 hours): deploy emergency edge rate limiter config targeting tenants with >20% retry growth; set per-tenant queue cap at proxy; enable immediate fastfail for requests exceeding queue_timeout=200ms
Mitigation (2-6 hours): apply proxy config to surface backpressure tokens to runtime via X-backpressure header; lower proxy default max_inflight to match runtime capacity for gen endpoints

Short-term fix (1-3 days): runtime patch to honour proxy admission headers and reject rather than silently queue when under eviction pressure; add early KV cache compaction trigger under steady high-queue conditions

Medium-term (2-6 weeks): implement adaptive admission control in runtime (feedback loop using runtime_queue_length, kvcache_eviction_rate, and observed p95) to refuse new requests or triage to low-cost model variants
Long-term (quarter): unify backpressure protocol between edge and runtime (binary token/lease) and expose per-tenant admission insights in Console
rollout_plan: Stage 0: Apply edge rate-limiter config with targeted tenants in us-west-2 (canary 10% traffic) and observe for 30 minutes
Stage 1: Patch runtime on a small subset of serving nodes in us-west-2 (canary 5 nodes) with admission-header handling for 4 hours
Stage 2: Expand runtime patch to 50% of nodes if canary success criteria met (no >2x 5xx increase), then to 100% over next 6 hours
Fallback: rollback runtime change immediately if error rate or latency exceeds threshold defined in runbook
Notify: send interim customer updates per escalation playbook at 30m, 2h, 6h, and close with a postmortem within 48h
postmortem_notes: Correlation observed between KV cache eviction spikes and head-of-line latency increases on generation requests
Proxy default max_inflight was provisioned higher than runtime admission targets after last scaling change (mismatch introduced during runtime autoscale refactor)
Retries were being generated by SDK clients due to TCP-level timeouts; increasing keepalive and reducing proxy queueing surface mitigated the amplification
Dedicated clusters with slower autoscale showed delay-based failures rather than immediate 5xx; solution needs to account for autoscale lag across deployment types
Private/on-prem customers with low egress caps require additional network-level mitigations (egress policing and smaller prefetch sizes)
Action item: add an egress/queueing column to tenant SLO dashboard and a per-tenant synthetic surge test in CI
